Private Sonoran Desert Sunset Tour from Scottsdale and Phoenix

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Sonoran Desert sunset tour from Scottsdale and Phoenix as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for the whole afternoon: the group is driven out to a preserve trailhead, waited on while it is out of the vehicle, then brought home. The published window is 4-5 hours and it bills 5 hours, so the afternoon starts at $625 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) and the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $725 before 8% tax — roughly $52 a seat with 14 aboard. Below: the row's own 7 steps, why this page prints no sunset time, which vehicle fits, and how the quote is built. Call (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

What is a private Sonoran Desert sunset tour from Scottsdale?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for your group for the window the row publishes as 4-5 hours, not a seat on somebody else's coach. 4 vehicles are offered for it, seating 6 to 14, and priced from $625 to $1,475. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport and nothing at the stops themselves. Your group decides who is aboard and how the booked hours are spent; the chauffeur drives out to the desert edge, waits while you are out of the vehicle, and brings everyone home. Nobody has to drive home into low sun. Per head the arithmetic is plainer than it looks. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter splits $725 across its seats, about $52 each; the 6-seat Luxury SUV (Suburban) splits $625 across 6, about $104. Those are the current published hourly rates carried across this window, never a fare sold per person.

What does the afternoon include, stop by stop?

The tour publishes 7 steps and states the window as 4-5 hours. 3 of them are written as conditional on purpose — the pickup, the viewpoint and the exit — because daylight and preserve access are decided by the city rather than by us. The row's own list is above, word for word. The conditional steps are the honest part, and here they are in full: "Afternoon pickup timed to current sunset and access", "Seasonal sunset viewpoint" and "Exit the preserve before the current trailhead closing time". None is dropped from a quote and none is turned into a promise about a clock this site does not publish. Inside the booked window an hourly charter buys time rather than mileage, so a stop written down before the date costs nothing extra. A group that would rather stay aboard the whole way can: the row's own walk step is written as "Short walk or accessible scenic stop", and the row leaves the choice between them to the group. When does the afternoon start, and when does it have to end?

That is the question every group asks first, and this page answers it by refusing to print a time. Sunset moves through the year and so do the gates, so the 5 requested hours are placed around the date you book rather than around a published departure slot. In the tour's own words: "Sunset time changes by date. The McDowell Sonoran Preserve is open from sunrise to sunset, and individual trailhead gate times change during the year. Check the City of Scottsdale's current hours, then submit an arrival and return window that allows the group to exit before closing." Read the last clause twice: you send the arrival and return window you want, and the desk confirms it against the vehicle you chose. That is why the row's last highlight is written as "Current preserve access checked" rather than as a guarantee.

Which vehicle fits the group on a desert sunset run?

Group size decides it, and nothing else does. Every row below prices the identical window: the published hourly rate times 5 billable hours, because 5 requested hours sit below the free-hour ladder, which starts at 7, against each unit's own 4-hour minimum. Up to 6 travellers the Luxury SUV (Suburban) runs the afternoon for $625, and it is the row's first recommendation — the smallest cabin of the 4 offered. The Executive Black Sprinter and Executive White Sprinter share a rate at $145 an hour and seat 14 each. The Maybach Jet Sprinter seats 9 at $295 an hour, which makes it the dearest row in this table at $1,475. The per-seat column divides the window total by seated capacity — friends splitting one fare. It is why the cheapest seat and the cheapest afternoon are different vehicles: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the least expensive booking at $625, while the Executive Black Sprinter carries the cheapest seat at $52. A party larger than 14 moves as one multi-vehicle booking. What does the afternoon cost, and what is not in it?

A booking in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $725 before 8% tax — $145 an hour across 5 billable hours. Split 14 ways that is roughly $52 a seat, and the least expensive vehicle runs the same window for $625. Three rules build every number: the window is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, 5 requested hours earn 0 free hours because the ladder starts at 7, and 8% tax is the only addition. Nothing is charged by the mile or per passenger. 50% is taken today by card, the balance 48 hours before pickup. What the fare excludes is short: anything charged at the stop, and food. Drinks travel; meals happen off the vehicle — "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." The afternoon starts at $625 and the table above tops out at $1,475; request a current quote for your date.

How much walking does the afternoon involve?

As much or as little as the group chooses — the tour sells the transportation and leaves the walking to you, which is the honest position when trail conditions and closures are set by the city rather than by a 5-hour transportation booking. The tour's own answer: "Choose a walk or drive-focused stop using current official access guidance, weather, daylight, and the group's mobility. Send the selected location for transportation review." So the practical step is the one the row asks for: send the stop you want and the window you want it in, and the booking is reviewed around it. A group with a walker, a stroller or a guest who would rather not leave the cabin is planning the same afternoon as everyone else.

What is worth stopping for out there, and will we see wildlife?

The row publishes 6 highlights for the afternoon, and they are the only ones this page names: McDowell Sonoran Preserve, Scenic Scottsdale desert route, Desert wildlife, Golden hour photography, Arizona sunset, Current preserve access checked. Each is somewhere the vehicle can wait while the group is out of it. The official City of Scottsdale pages behind that list are cited at the foot of this article; this page lifts no hour, fee or rule from them, and it adds no place the row does not already name. On the animals the tour is equally plain: "Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed. Check current preserve guidance, keep a safe distance from animals, and plan the stop around weather and daylight." What a chauffeured afternoon adds is the waiting: nobody hunts for a parking space and nobody drives home afterwards.

Where can the afternoon start, what should we bring, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in Scottsdale or Phoenix — or any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page — not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things: the date, the headcount and one address. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address for the whole party and one phone we call keeps a group together at the start of an afternoon whose end is set by the light rather than by us. Bags have a published cap per vehicle rather than a house rule: the Maybach Jet Sprinter takes 4, the Executive Black Sprinter 40, and every unit this tour offers carries an owner-confirmed number, so nothing here is a guess. Camera cases and anything oversized are confirmed in writing before the date. The chauffeur is a resource: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Call Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339 for anything the form cannot price.
